110.title: Relation of Adjusters to Individual Mortals
110.b0.ask: “How does the spirit of God within my mind lead me toward eternity while still respecting my freedom?”
110.b2.p: In Papers 107 through 109 we looked at where the Thought Adjuster comes from, what its nature is, and what career it follows in the universe. Paper 110 now turns to the Adjuster’s relationship with one person — the individual mortal.
110.b3.p: The author says that giving freedom to imperfect beings brings inevitable tragedy, but the perfect God shares those sufferings in loving companionship. And he confesses that the devotion of an Adjuster to the individual is the most truly divine affection in all creation; nothing in the universe of universes is quite comparable to it.
110.b4.p: What, then, does this divine indweller do within our minds? And how does it work together with our free will to lead us to eternal fusion?
110.b8.p: The Adjuster does not live in the physical brain; it indwells the mortal mind. Even when we do not notice it, it is constantly communicating with us, especially in those moments when the mind makes worshipful contact with spirit in the superconsciousness. The author calls the Adjusters tireless toilers, safe and sure guides, and patient teachers, and he wishes we could love them more and co-operate with them more fully.
110.b9.p: The Adjuster’s chief concern is our spiritual preparation for the next stage, yet it is not indifferent to our health, happiness, and true prosperity. It stays with us through every disaster and sickness that does not destroy the mind. That is why deliberately polluting the body — and poisoning the mind — so greatly hinders its work.
110.b10.t: Greatly retard its efforts to lift up the material mind
Fear, anger, envy, jealousy, suspicion, and intolerance interfere with the soul’s spiritual progress
110.b11.p: Today we are passing through the period of the courtship of our Adjuster. If we are faithful to this trust, there will at last come fusion — a oneness so perfect that even the most experienced personalities can never tell the two partners apart.
110.b13.p: When the Adjuster comes to us, it brings a model career, an ideal life plan. But no human being is obliged to accept that plan. We are all subjects of predestination, yet it is not foreordained that we must accept it. No one will ever be spiritualized against his will; survival is a gift that must be desired.
110.b14.p: The Adjuster is not trying to control our thinking but to spiritualize and eternalize it; directly influencing thought is our own personality prerogative. The Adjuster is devoted to building up a spiritual counterpart of our life, a morontia transcript of our true advancing self. When our mind comes into line with the Adjuster’s mind and our will carries out its decisions, the Adjuster’s prepersonal will finds personal expression through our choice.
110.b15.t: A personal creature — mind and will
A prepersonal creature — premind and prewill
A dual mind dominated by one will — the approach to morontia mind
110.b17.p: The Adjuster’s message is usually lost in the material currents of the mind; only now and then do we catch a faint and distant echo of the divine voice. Its success depends less on the theories of our beliefs than on our decisions, determinations, and steadfast faith. The secret of survival is the supreme desire to be Godlike, together with the willingness to do whatever that desire requires. The Adjuster itself never fails.
110.b18.p: This co-operation does not mean self-torture or mock piety; the ideal life is one of loving service rather than fearful apprehension. Confusion, discouragement, ignorance, and doubt cannot prevent survival. Only conscious resistance to the Adjuster’s leading can do that. The author names four ways we can consciously increase our harmony with the Adjuster.
110.b19.t: Basing life on truth, beauty, and goodness
Recognizing his fatherhood and worshiping him in love
Recognizing the brotherhood of man and sincerely serving our fellows
Recognizing our obligations to the Supreme Being — the birth of cosmic morality
110.b20.h: 4. The Adjuster’s Work in the Mind
110.b21.p: The Adjuster is in full touch with the intelligence of the universes, but because our natures have so little in common, it can pass on very little of that wisdom to us. We cannot tell the products of our own intellect from those of the Adjuster’s work. Most sudden thoughts are simply ideas rising from the submerged levels of the mind; the revelations of the Adjuster come through the superconscious, not the subconscious.
110.b22.p: The Urantia races are so largely electrically and chemically controlled, and so emotional, that the Adjusters find them exceedingly hard to guide. Even a flash of new truth can set off fanaticism or an intellectual upheaval, and many a strange “ism” has arisen from garbled Adjuster communications. The records show that in each generation fewer people could function safely with self-acting Adjusters, and the planetary supervisors favor proposals to preserve the higher spiritual types of the races.
110.b24.p: We must not confuse the Adjuster with conscience. Conscience is a human and purely psychic reaction. Conscience admonishes us to do right; the Adjuster, in addition, tries to tell us what truly is right.
110.b25.t: Tries to tell us what truly is right
110.b26.p: It is also dangerous to treat dreams as the Adjuster’s voice. Disordered dreams actually show the Adjuster’s failure to harmonize the mind, and ordinary dreams are purely physiologic and psychologic. It is likewise dangerous to take every new idea as the Adjuster’s dictation. It is better to err by taking an Adjuster’s expression for a human experience than to raise a human reaction to divine dignity.
110.b29.p: On a material world, personality realization lies in conquering the seven psychic circles one after another. Entering the seventh circle marks the beginning of true personality function; completing the first marks relative mortal maturity. Mastering the circles is not fusion itself, but it prepares the way for it. Passing through them requires balanced growth of body, mind, and spirit; when intellect outruns spirit, or spirit develops too one-sidedly, communication with the Adjuster becomes difficult and dangerous.
110.b30.p: Every decision we make either impedes or helps the Adjuster’s work. Not only the weight of a decision matters, but also its repetition. Mastery of the circles shows itself in three ways.
110.b31.t: The mind draws nearer the Adjuster in proportion to circle attainment
The emergence of the morontia soul shows the extent of mastery
Persons become more real as they ascend the circles
110.b32.t: Moral choice develops and the Adjuster is received — a potential citizen of the local universe
A personal seraphic guardian is assigned, and the Adjuster’s work becomes much more effective
Relative mortal maturity; some direct communication with the Adjuster
110.b33.p: Circle attainment is only relatively related to God-consciousness. A seventh circler can know God and be conscious of sonship almost as truly as a first circler. The quality of the soul depends wholly on how living faith grasps the fact that we are sons of God. The great days in an Adjuster’s career are when its subject breaks into the third circle, when he reaches the first, and when the two are at last fused forever.
110.b35.p: Completing the seven circles is not the same as fusion. Fusion depends on a final and complete attunement of the mortal will with the will of God. When this happens during physical life, the body is consumed at once, and onlookers would see the mortal vanish “⟦Q 110:7.2⟧in chariots of fire.⟦/Q⟧” After fusion, Adjuster and soul become one entity, each possessing all the experience and values of the other.
110.b36.p: For most of us, though, the Adjuster must patiently await the deliverance of death, for the ear of the human mind is almost deaf to the messages of love the Adjuster translates. The author closes with the plea an Adjuster once sent to its human partner in the reserve corps of destiny: it promised to be faithful to the very end, and begged him to survive and not to disappoint it.
110.b39.p: Paper 110 shows us the Adjuster within us at close range. It comes with a perfect plan, yet it never overrides our will; it works only through our decisions and our faith. Its voice is easily confused with conscience, dreams, or any passing thought, so humble discernment is needed — but neither confusion nor ignorance can block survival; only conscious resistance can. As we rise through the psychic circles by repeated decisions, the Adjuster impresses itself ever more clearly on our minds, until at last in fusion the two become one forever. And all of this finally rests on our own choice.
110.b40.t: The Adjuster indwells the mind, not the brain, and cares about our whole life
The Adjuster brings a perfect plan but is always subservient to our will
Only conscious resistance can prevent survival
4. The Adjuster’s Work in the Mind
The Adjuster’s revelations come through the superconscious, not the subconscious
Do not take conscience or dreams for the Adjuster’s voice
Repeated decisions carry us up the circles into closer attunement
Fusion comes through the full attunement of the mortal will with God’s will
110.b42.box: The Adjuster respects our freedom to the very end, and it becomes one with us as fully as we choose its will.
111.title: The Adjuster and the Soul
111.b0.ask: “What is the soul that is born where God’s spirit meets my mind — and how does it grow?”
111.b2.p: In Paper 110 we saw how the Adjuster works within the mind of the individual mortal. Paper 111 now moves on to the fruit of that partnership: the soul that is born and grows between the Adjuster and the human mind.
111.b3.p: Because the Adjuster dwells in the mind, neither science nor philosophy can ever fully understand the human soul. The soul is the child of the universe and can be known only through cosmic insight and spiritual discovery. The idea of a soul and an indwelling spirit is not new; it appears in many faiths — the Hindu atman, the Chinese yang and yin, the Egyptian ka and ba. Many Egyptians even believed that the ka was “⟦Q 111:0.6⟧an oracle from God in everybody.⟦/Q⟧”
111.b4.p: What, then, is the soul exactly? And what part do our choices and our inner life play in its growth?
111.b8.p: The Adjuster’s work is spiritual, yet it must all be done on an intellectual foundation. Mind is the human soil in which the Adjuster, with the co-operation of the personality, grows the morontia soul. Material mind is the arena where we live, make decisions, choose God or forsake him, and either eternalize or destroy ourselves.
111.b9.p: Evolution gave us a body, and the Father gave us the Adjuster, but mind has been placed in our own hands; it is by mind that we live or die. What matters is not so much what the mind understands now as what it desires to understand — not so much what we are today as what we are becoming day by day. The Adjusters manipulate the mind but never dominate it against our will.
111.b10.t: The morontia harbors of eternal survival, and at last the Paradise Father
111.b12.p: The material mind is a cosmic loom. On the morontia fabric it carries, the Adjuster threads the patterns of a character of enduring values and divine meanings — and that character is the surviving soul. The relationship of mind and spirit is not a simple mixture of the two; it produces something entirely new and unique.
111.b13.t: The three antecedents of the soul
The mind itself and all the cosmic influences acting on it
The Adjuster and all the spiritual influences in human life
Neither material nor spiritual but morontial — this is the soul
111.b14.p: The midway creatures have long called this soul the “mid-mind,” standing between the material mind below and the cosmic mind above. The soul is the joint offspring of a mind led by a human will that craves to know God, working together with the Adjuster, an actual fragment of God.
111.b16.p: The mistakes of the mind and wrong conduct can delay the soul’s growth, but they cannot stop it once it has begun. Still, the mortal keeps the power to cancel that choice and reject survival; until fusion with the Adjuster, one can forsake the Father’s will. During life the will resides in the circuits of the material mind, but as we grow it identifies more and more with the soul, and after resurrection it is wholly identified with the morontia self.
111.b17.p: The mortal career is not so much a probation as an education. The mind knows quantity and meaning, but quality — value — is felt. As the soul is filled with truth, beauty, and goodness, it becomes indestructible.
111.b20.p: Recognition fits sense impressions into memory patterns; understanding organizes them into a network of principles; and meanings arise from the two together. Meanings and values are perceived only in the inner, supermaterial realm of experience. All the advances of true civilization are born in this inner world; it is only the inner life that is truly creative.
111.b21.t: Its creativity is most subject to our direction
Materialistic pursuits alone cannot advance it
The birthplace of all true progress
111.b22.p: Today the nations are led by people with an abundance of ideas but a poverty of ideals, and this explains poverty, divorce, war, and racial hatred. Creativity can also turn into destructiveness: evil is a partiality of creativity, and every conflict is a kind of civil war in the personality. The past cannot be changed, but the future can be changed by the present creativity of the inner self.
111.b24.p: Doing the will of God is simply showing our willingness to share our inner life with God. Sharing is Godlike. And God shared first: he entrusted a part of himself to live within us, and consented to indwell us subject to the human will.
111.b25.p: So choosing the Father’s will is not a surrender of will. It is a consecration of will, an expansion of will, and a perfecting of will.
111.b26.t: “⟦Q 111:5.6|109:6.5|136:4.4⟧Not my will but yours be done⟦/Q⟧”
“⟦Q 111:5.6|118:8.11⟧It is my will that your will be done⟦/Q⟧”
Fusion with the Adjuster — an eternal partnership of the will of man and the will of God
111.b28.p: Man is a part of nature and bound by it, yet he can rise above it; he is finite, yet indwelt by a spark of infinity. Because of this double position, the courage that conquers nature can turn into the temptation of self-pride. But finiteness itself is not evil. Evil and sin arise from the misuse, distortion, and perversion of the finite.
111.b29.p: We can find the love of God without facts, and the laws of God without love, but we cannot appreciate the infinite harmony of God until we have unified divine law and divine love in our own experience. The insecurity we feel in this paradox is natural, and only living faith can sustain us. Of all the dangers to our spiritual integrity, pride is the greatest.
111.b30.t: Triumphant over nature and all things finite
Self-pride and the deifying of self-consciousness
111.b32.p: Uncertainty with security is the essence of the Paradise adventure: uncertain in time and in mind, but secure in spirit and in eternity, trusting the Father’s love. The Adjuster cannot stop our struggles or lessen the hardships of life, but if we allow it, it will fight with us and for us, and keep showing us the real purpose of all our uphill effort.
111.b33.p: The races of Urantia are a complex blend of many stocks, and this makes the work of Adjusters and seraphim harder. One guardian of destiny testified that in her subject ambition fought against indolence, high purpose against primitive urges, and faith against fear without end. Yet because of the Adjuster’s ever-present help, that soul achieved a fair degree of happiness and success and has now ascended to the mansion worlds.
111.b35.p: Paper 111 calmly explains where the soul comes from. Evolution gave us our bodies and the Father gave us the Adjuster, but mind was placed in our own hands. On the loom of that mind, our choices and the Adjuster’s labor meet to weave a new reality: the soul. The soul grows in the inner life — the home of ideals and creativity, but also the place where pride and destructiveness lie in wait. Choosing the Father’s will does not mean giving up our will but consecrating and enlarging it. The Adjuster does not remove life’s hardships, yet it fights the battle with us and leads us safely home.
111.b36.t: Mind is the ship, the Adjuster the pilot, the will the captain
The soul is a morontia reality born of the relationship of mind and spirit
Mortal life is not a probation but an education
True creativity and ideals are born only in the inner life
Choosing the Father’s will is not surrender but consecration
Bound by nature yet rising above it, man’s greatest danger is pride
The Adjuster does not remove our hardships, but it fights with us
111.b38.box: The soul is the fabric of eternity woven by our choices and the Adjuster’s labor, and our will is never more whole than when it chooses the Father’s will.
112.title: Personality Survival
112.b0.ask: “When death takes away the body and the mind, what part of me survives — and how do I awaken again?”
112.b2.p: In Papers 110 and 111 we saw how the Adjuster works in the mind and how the soul grows out of that partnership. Paper 112 now comes to the greatest threshold of the journey: death and survival.
112.b3.p: Urantia is our starting point, and through every stage of growth there is one part of us that remains absolutely unaltered: personality, permanence in the presence of change. The author says it would be presumptuous to define personality, yet he lists fourteen things that are known about it. Even a few of them show what a unique gift personality is.
112.b4.p: How, then, does personality pass through death? And what survives to awaken again on the mansion worlds?
112.b8.t: The Universal Father himself, or the Conjoint Actor acting for him
Not wholly subject to the fetters of antecedent causation
Changeless in the presence of change
It can dedicate its free will to doing the will of God
Absolutely unique; persons are associable but not addable
It may survive death with identity in the surviving soul
112.b9.p: Personality is a potentially eternal endowment, designed to function from the lowly finite to the very borders of the absolute. Finite personality has three dimensions — length, depth, and breadth — and the personality given to Urantia mortals has a potential of seven dimensions in all.
112.b10.t: The direction of progression — evolution; it denotes meaning
Drives and self-realization; it signifies value
Co-ordination and the organization of selfhood; it embraces insight
112.b11.p: Life is a process taking place between the organism and its environment, and personality gives that relationship identity and continuity. Man is innately a social creature and cannot function well in isolation. In aggregations parts are added; in systems parts are arranged — and in the human system it is personality that unifies all activities.
112.b14.p: The fact that God became man has forever changed all the meanings and values of human personality. True love is the mutual regard of whole personalities. Having personality at all marks man as a spiritual being; the very fact that a materialist can deny supermaterial reality shows that cosmic consciousness is at work in his mind. The observer cannot be the thing observed.
112.b15.t: The human self observes the material world
Realizes in experience the cosmic reality behind the observation of the observation
112.b16.p: A self that can survive death evolves only by moving the seat of identity from the material body to the immortal morontia soul. This transfer is brought about by the sincerity, persistence, and steadfastness of our God-seeking decisions.
112.b18.p: We usually think of only one kind of death, the stopping of bodily life. But in relation to personality survival there are really three kinds.
112.b19.t: Survival is finally rejected — though the body lives on, the person is cosmically dead
The circuits of the willing mind are irreparably destroyed — the soul may survive according to earlier choices
When the brain’s vital pulsations cease, the Adjuster leaves for Divinington
112.b20.p: After death the body returns to the elements, but two nonmaterial factors continue. The Adjuster goes to Divinington carrying the memory transcription of our life, and the immortal soul remains in the keeping of the destiny guardian. On the mansion worlds the two are reunited, and we awaken. The Adjuster temporarily loses personality but not identity; the human loses identity but not personality. Those who have gone on cannot send messages back to their loved ones; such communication is forbidden in the present dispensation.
112.b22.p: When death comes, the Adjuster bids farewell and departs for Divinington. The Universal Censors are able to obtain an epitome of the life from the Adjuster’s transcription, and this, together with the seraphic records, is used in judgment. What follows depends on whether the mortal ascends individually or awaits the group summons at the end of the dispensation.
112.b23.t: Temporary assignments of a waiting Adjuster (by choice)
Joining the vanished Monitors for undisclosed service
Enrolling in a training school of Divinington
Serving as a student observer on another of the Father’s sacred spheres
Messenger service for the Personalized Adjusters
Choosing worlds for further service, in case the human partner has rejected survival
112.b24.p: If someone has reached the third circle or higher and has a personal guardian, and if the records of Adjuster and seraphim agree and are confirmed by the Censors, the soul is decreed to pass at once to the resurrection halls of the mansion worlds. The Adjuster then goes to the presence of the Paradise Father, returns, and is ready to meet the soul on the third period.
112.b26.p: Personality that comes from the Father is eternal, but as to identity it is a conditioned eternal reality: man must choose whether or not he will be present when that destiny is reached. An energy system has no choice, but man has everything to do with his own destiny. The Adjuster is truly the path to Paradise, but we must walk that path by our own free choice.
112.b27.t: The integrity of the human will, for eternal destiny
The sincerity of mortal free will, for eternal personality
The faithfulness of mortal choice, for a new ascending son
The steadfastness and wisdom of decision-actions, for experiential evolution
112.b28.p: Those who fail to master the circles through no fault of their own are given an extension of probation, and whenever there is doubt, the universe governments always rule in the individual’s interest. This does not mean a second chance after rejecting the first, but every will creature will have one true opportunity to make an undoubted and final choice.
112.b30.p: What survives death is the soul — the child born of the human you working together with the divine you, the Adjuster. From death to repersonalization the soul is wholly unconscious, kept by the seraphic guardian. In the resurrection halls a morontia form is prepared, the Adjuster returns, and the seraphim bestow the soul upon that form; then repersonalization is complete. Memories without spiritual meaning perish with the brain, but the memory of relationships between persons has cosmic value and will persist.
112.b32.p: As a butterfly emerges from the caterpillar, our true personalities will appear for the first time on the mansion worlds. In physical life someone may be outwardly beautiful though inwardly unlovely, but in the morontia life the form increasingly reflects the inner person, and on spirit levels outer form and inner nature approach complete identity.
112.b33.p: The mortal intellect perishes, but its meanings and values do not, and the creature’s will persists despite the loss of the material intellect. For the memory patterns in the soul to come alive at once, the returning Adjuster is needed. Those who ascend without Adjusters must recover their memories over a long time with the help of seraphim.
112.b34.t: The seven adjutant mind-spirits under the spirit of wisdom
Direct contact with cosmic mind as modified by the Divine Minister
The direct ministry of the cosmic mind of Orvonton
112.b36.p: Fusion gives personality eternal actualities: fixed divinity quality, past-eternity experience and memory, and immortality. It usually takes place while the ascender is in the local system, and once fusion has occurred, there can be no future danger to the eternal career. Fusion never happens until the superuniverse has declared that the human has made a final and irrevocable choice for the eternal career.
112.b37.t: A secure universe value, witnessed by fusion
112.b38.p: The Adjuster has not won personality, nor has the human acquired immortality, on his own; together they have become a new ascending personality. No event of time or eternity can ever separate them, and their Paradise home is Ascendington, not Divinington. With fusion the Father has fulfilled his promise of the gift of himself, and fused finaliters are expected to help administer the universes of outer space.
112.b41.p: Paper 112 shows death not as an end but as a threshold. Personality, unchanging amid all change, is the Father’s gift, but whether it takes part in its eternal destiny is our choice. At death the Adjuster departs with our memories, the soul sleeps in the guardian’s care, and on the mansion worlds the two meet again to awaken us. What has no spiritual meaning passes away, but our relationships with those we have loved remain. The universe governments show mercy so that everyone has one true opportunity, and when at last we are fused forever with the Adjuster, the partnership of God and man becomes a oneness no one can undo.
112.b42.t: Personality is the Father’s gift, unchanging amid all change
The surviving self moves its seat of identity from the body to the soul
There are three kinds of death: spiritual, intellectual, and physical
The Adjuster keeps our memories and prepares for reunion
Personality is eternal, but we choose whether to share its destiny
On the mansion worlds our true personality emerges like a butterfly
In fusion God and man become forever inseparable
112.b44.box: What survives death is the soul we and the Adjuster bring forth together — and if we truly desire it, the heritage of the ages is ours.
113.title: Seraphic Guardians of Destiny
113.b0.ask: “Who is the guardian angel who stays beside me all my life, and how does that angel walk with me even beyond death?”
113.b2.p: In Papers 110 through 112 we looked at the Thought Adjuster who indwells us, the soul that grows through our partnership with the Adjuster, and survival beyond death. Now Paper 113 introduces another companion — one who works from outside us, yet is always at our side: the seraphic guardian of destiny.
113.b3.p: Seraphim are the traditional angels of heaven, and they have ministered on Urantia since the earliest times of human intelligence. In past ages these destiny guardians were about the only group of angels that had recognition here, and in many a revelation “⟦Q 113:0.1⟧the word was spoken by angels.⟦/Q⟧” The paper itself is presented by the Chief of Seraphim stationed on Urantia.
113.b4.p: How, then, are guardian angels assigned? How does their work differ from that of the Adjuster? And what part do they play in death, in resurrection, and on the long road to Paradise?
113.b8.p: The teaching about guardian angels is not a myth. Jesus himself said that the angels of the little ones do always behold the presence of the spirit of his Father. Originally the seraphim were assigned to the separate races of Urantia, but since the bestowal of Michael they are assigned in accordance with human intelligence, spirituality, and destiny.
113.b9.t: One company of seraphim, with one battalion of cherubim, ministers to them
Grouped in seven classes according to the circles they have attained
Personal seraphim are assigned the moment they enroll in a reserve corps of destiny
113.b10.p: For those of normal mind, the care grows closer as they move inward through the circles. When a person reaches the third circle, a personal angel — in reality two — is henceforth wholly and exclusively devoted to that one human being.
113.b11.t: One guardian angel watches over a thousand mortals
A seraphic pair guides them in groups of five hundred
A pair of seraphim takes charge of about one hundred
A pair of seraphim takes charge of ten
A personal pair of angels is wholly devoted to one person
113.b13.p: Seraphim are called guardians of destiny only when they are assigned to a human soul who has made a supreme decision to become Godlike, has entered the third circle, or has been mustered into a reserve corps of destiny. The first mortal on Urantia to receive a personal guardian was Rantowoc, a wise man of the red race of long ago. All such assignments are made from volunteering seraphim, and only those of long service — the more experienced and tested types — become destiny guards.
113.b14.p: The angels develop an abiding affection for their human associates, and they share most of our emotions. The one feeling they find hard to understand is the legacy of animal fear. They cannot easily see why we let our higher intellectual powers, even our religious faith, be so dominated by fear.
113.b15.t: Serves for the remainder of the life of that human being
Becomes the recorder of the undertaking — the recording angel of the evolutionary worlds
113.b17.p: One of the most important things a guardian does is to bring a personal co-ordination to the many impersonal spirit influences that surround and impinge on a human mind. It is exceedingly difficult for nonpersonal spirits to make direct contact with such material and personal minds. The Adjuster is the presence of the Father, and the Spirit of Truth the presence of the Sons; the seraphim unify these divine endowments on the lower levels of human spiritual experience.
113.b18.t: Co-ordinators who make impersonal ministries personal
Correlators of mind and morontia — interpreters
They manipulate the environment with the physical controllers and the midway creatures
113.b19.p: This is why the seraphim become the custodians of the mind patterns, memory formulas, and soul realities of a survivor between death and resurrection. How can an angel created but a little above the level of humanity do such complex things? The author admits that they do not really know, but conjectures that this ministry is made possible by the unrevealed working of the Supreme Being.
113.b21.p: Seraphim are mind stimulators. They continually seek to promote circle-making decisions in the human mind. Yet they do not work as the Adjuster does, from within and through the soul. They work from the outside inward, through the social, ethical, and moral environment of human beings.
113.b22.t: A fragment of the Universal Father
The personal agency of the ministry of the Infinite Spirit
From outside inward, through the environment
The essence of man’s eternal nature
The teacher of man’s evolving nature
113.b23.p: To accept the guidance of a seraphim rarely means attaining a life of ease. Following it, we are sure to meet the rugged hills of moral choosing and spiritual progress. The impulse of worship comes largely from the higher adjutants and the Adjuster, but the urge to pray very often arises from seraphic influence. Adjusters and seraphim seem to have no communication with each other, yet they always work in perfect harmony, and the guardians are most active when the Adjusters are least active.
113.b25.p: Angels do not invade the sanctity of the human mind, they do not manipulate our will, and they do not directly contact the indwelling Adjusters. No order of universe personality has power to curtail the prerogatives of human choosing. Still, they care for us so feelingly that, figuratively, they “⟦Q 113:5.2⟧weep because of your willful intolerance and stubbornness.⟦/Q⟧”
113.b26.p: The seraphim are guardians, not rulers. We must chart our own course, and then they act to make the best possible use of the course we have chosen. They are not directly concerned with our appeals or prayers; they carry out the mandates of their superiors. They step into the human drama only in emergencies, or in rare cases when vital links in the chain of human evolution are in jeopardy.
113.b29.p: When a mortal dies, the destiny guardian faithfully conserves the records, the identity specifications, and the soul — everything that constitutes the real you, except the identity carried by the departing Adjuster. The guardian reports to her superiors, then proceeds to the first mansion world and waits there for her former ward to awaken.
113.b30.t: Keeps the survival values of the slumbering soul and repersonalizes you
Is the identity of the immortal being — it will identify you
Is newly fabricated in the resurrection halls
113.b31.p: When a planetary age ends, it is the group guardians who reassemble those of the lower circles in the resurrection halls. For those who do not survive, the seraphim answer the roll call but the Adjusters make no answer; this is the formal recognition of the cessation of creature existence. This roll call of justice always follows the roll call of mercy. The guardians in Satania who went astray in the Lucifer rebellion are detained on Jerusem until the final adjudication, and the souls once entrusted to them are kept safe by volunteer seconaphim.
113.b33.p: The first awakening on the mansion world is a real resurrection. There, for the first time, we actually see the angelic companions who were always with us on earth, and we become truly conscious of the divine Monitor who indwelt our minds. Our first assignment in the morontia life will be as assistants to the seraphim.
113.b34.t: How the guardians go with us
Open companions who witness the decrees of our union with the Adjuster
They go with us through the worlds of system and constellation progress
They pilot us through the Melchizedeks to the Sovereign of all Nebadon
They stay with us to Uversa, until we enseconaphim for the Havona flight
Some go with us; others pass through Seraphington and wait for us on the shores of Paradise
113.b35.p: The bonds formed on the worlds of human origin are never forgotten. Only destiny guardians are mustered into the mortal Corps of the Finality. On Seraphington the two angels achieve spirit two-in-oneness and gain a new capacity for fusion with a fragment of the Paradise Father. So some of our loving seraphic associates in time become our finaliter associates in eternity.
113.b37.p: Paper 113 shows us the companion who was always beside us, though we never saw her. The Adjuster works within to build our eternal nature; the guardian seraphim works from outside, through our surroundings, to teach our evolving nature. The angels never invade our will; they only make the best of the course we ourselves have chosen. When death comes, they hold the values of our soul and wake us again on the mansion world, and after that they walk with us all the way to the gates of Paradise. Guiding one soul to those gates is the most honored path open to a seraphim, and so the companion of time becomes the comrade of eternity.
113.b38.t: As we move inward through the circles, guardian care becomes more personal
An experienced pair of volunteer seraphim cares for one person to the end
Seraphim personally co-ordinate the impersonal spirit influences
The Adjuster works within; the seraphim work from outside, through the environment
Angels are not overlords but simply guardians
The guardian keeps the soul and repersonalizes it at the resurrection
The guardian angel of time becomes the finaliter associate of eternity
113.b40.box: The guardian angel respects our choices, stays beside us all our life, and walks with us beyond death to the very gates of Paradise.
114.title: Seraphic Planetary Government
114.b0.ask: “Urantia has been isolated by rebellion — so who governs it, unseen, and how?”
114.b2.p: In Paper 113 we met the guardian of destiny who stays beside one person. Now Paper 114 widens the view and shows how seraphim care for and help govern a whole planet. The Most Highs rule in the kingdoms of men through many celestial forces, but chiefly through the ministry of seraphim.
114.b3.p: The author, the Chief of Seraphim, reports that at noon on the day of writing the roll call on Urantia showed more than five hundred million pairs of seraphim. Yet the government of Urantia is unlike that of any other world in Nebadon. The reasons are unusual: Urantia is a life modification planet; it was caught up in the Lucifer rebellion and the Adamic default; it was a bestowal world of Michael; and it holds an archangels’ circuit.
114.b4.p: With neither a Planetary Prince nor an Adam, under whose care does this isolated world now stand? And why need we never feel abandoned?
114.b8.p: The sovereignty of Urantia was first held in trust by the sovereign of the Satania system, who delegated it to a joint commission of Melchizedeks and Life Carriers. After the downfall of Caligastia, the planet had no settled relationship with the local universe until Michael completed his bestowal in the flesh and was proclaimed Planetary Prince of Urantia. That proclamation forever settled the status of our world.
114.b9.p: Yet Michael did not take up the personal administration of the planet. Instead he established a Jerusem commission of twenty-four former Urantians. More recently Machiventa Melchizedek has been named vicegerent Planetary Prince, but he has made not the slightest move to change the present regime. Opinions differ about when he will come; the narrator himself looks for Melchizedek’s appearance any day or hour.
114.b11.p: Since Michael’s bestowal, the general management of Urantia has been entrusted to these twenty-four onetime Urantians on Jerusem. All of them were real leaders when they lived here, and (except for Machiventa) their gifts of leadership have been further strengthened by mansion world experience and Jerusem training. When the council meets on Jerusem, its chairman is John, known to us as “the Baptist.”
114.b12.t: Gabriel of Salvington, in accordance with the mandate of Michael
114.b13.p: This commission also acts as advisory supervisors of the thirty-six other rebellion-isolated worlds of the system, but they are especially concerned with the welfare of the mortal races of Urantia. How long they will serve is unknown. It depends on some change in planetary status — the end of a dispensation, the final adjudication of the rebellion, or the reappearance of Michael.
114.b15.p: Every one hundred years of Urantia time, one of the twenty-four is sent to live on our world as resident governor general. While these papers were being prepared, the twentieth succeeded the nineteenth. His name is withheld only because mortal man is so prone to venerate, even to deify, his extraordinary superiors.
114.b16.p: The governor general has no personal authority of his own, yet he hands down scores of rulings each day which are accepted as final. He is much more of a fatherly adviser than a technical ruler. The angels regard him as their co-ordinating director, and the United Midwayers look upon him as their planetary father.
114.b18.p: Shortly after the Lucifer rebellion the government of Norlatiadek seized planetary authority, and so a Vorondadek Son still lives here as observer for the Most Highs of Edentia. The present observer is the twenty-third. He also serves as advisory director to the race commissioners.
114.b19.p: In a crisis, this Vorondadek Son would be the actual head of the government, except in purely spiritual matters. At his discretion he may seize the planetary government and act as Most High regent, and this has happened thirty-three times in Urantia’s history. In purely spiritual matters, supreme authority seems to rest with the commanding archangel of the archangels’ divisional headquarters on Urantia.
114.b21.p: Urantia has no formal government with separate legislative, executive, and judicial departments. What is missing is partly made up by other beings.
114.b22.t: The governor general, with the veto power held by the Most High observer
No absolutely authoritative judicial powers — only the conciliating commissions
In place of the Planetary Prince
The triune presence of the archangels, the Most High observer, and the governor general
In place of the Adamic regime
The special ministry of seraphim and the services of the midway creatures
114.b23.p: This loosely organized government works better than one might expect, thanks to the archangels’ circuit. Technically the planet is still spiritually isolated, but since the Spirit of Truth was poured out upon all flesh, that isolation is of little concern to individual mortals. Each administrative day begins with a consultative conference attended by the governor general, the planetary chief of archangels, the Most High observer, and others.
114.b24.h: 6. The Master Seraphim of Planetary Supervision
114.b25.p: When the first governor general arrived, at the same time as the outpouring of the Spirit of Truth, he brought with him twelve corps of special seraphim, graduates of Seraphington, who were at once assigned to planetary service. The author presides over the council of their twelve chiefs as planetary chief of seraphim.
114.b26.t: Fit the affairs of each generation into the mosaic of its age
Initiate the evolutionary progress of the social ages
“⟦Q 114:6.7⟧The angels of the churches⟦/Q⟧” — carry moral values safely from one epoch to the next
“⟦Q 114:6.8⟧The angels of the trumpets⟦/Q⟧” — political life and international relations
Conserve the evolutionary races, working with the race commissioners
Forecast a future age and plan for it — the architects of the eras
Mental and moral training, from the individual to whole races
Help those who promote health and prevent disease
Preserve and advance the home, the basic institution of civilization
Foster industrial development and better economic conditions
Foster the values of play, humor, and rest
“⟦Q 114:6.16⟧The angels of the angels⟦/Q⟧” — serve all other superhuman life on the planet
114.b27.p: The progress angels and the religious guardians check each other, keeping a balance between the new and the preserved. None of these angelic groups exercise direct or arbitrary control over their domains; they manipulate conditions to influence them favorably. They cannot inject new conceptions into human minds, but they often intensify some higher ideal that has already appeared there.
114.b29.p: The reserve corps of destiny consists of living men and women who have been admitted to special service in the superhuman administration of world affairs. Personal destiny guardians are appointed to them, and all of them have self-conscious Adjusters. Urantia has twelve reserve corps, one for each group of master seraphim, now totaling 962 persons. Except for less than a score of them, they are wholly unconscious of their preparation.
114.b30.t: They can be secretly rehearsed for possible emergency missions
They serve a cause without human recognition or reward
Their Adjuster has probable experience with earlier planetary crises
114.b31.p: These reservists are little known except in rare social and spiritual emergencies, when they act to prevent the breakdown of evolutionary culture or the extinction of the light of living truth. The corps was largest in the days of the Adamites and Andites, reached its low point around the time of Pentecost, and has steadily increased since then.
114.b32.p: We can have only a meager idea of an ideal planetary government, yet compared with the other isolated worlds our governments have not been so inferior. Above all, our world is not forgotten. From Uversa to Salvington, even in Havona and on Paradise, they all know we are here.
114.b35.p: Paper 114 shows that Urantia, though left without its Planetary Prince and its Adam, has never been neglected. Michael has been proclaimed its Planetary Prince, and the twenty-four counselors of Jerusem, the resident governor general, the Most High observer, and the archangels fill the empty places. The twelve corps of master seraphim quietly care for every area of human life — the age, religion, the nation, the home, health, education, even play — without force, while the reserve corps of destiny stands ready, unseen, for times of crisis. Beneath all this supervision lies one assurance: we are cherished as much as the children of worlds that were never betrayed, even more so.
114.b36.t: Michael is the Planetary Prince, and Machiventa has been named vicegerent Prince
Twenty-four former Urantians supervise the planet from Jerusem
One of them lives here for a century at a time as a fatherly adviser
In a crisis, the Vorondadek observer may take over as regent
The archangels’ circuit and many beings make up for a government without form
6. The Master Seraphim of Planetary Supervision
Twelve corps of seraphim care for every area of human life
Unknown men and women guard civilization against breakdown
115.title: The Supreme Being
115.b0.ask: “Why would a perfect God have a Deity who is still growing?”
115.b2.p: Paper 115 is one of the densest papers in the whole Urantia Book. Unfamiliar terms come one after another, but they all point toward a single question. If there is a perfect and infinite God, why is there also another Deity who is not yet complete, who is still growing?
115.b3.p: The very first lines give us a clue to the answer. With God the Father, sonship is the great relationship. With God the Supreme, achievement is the prerequisite to status — one must do something as well as be something. Here lies the reason why none of our striving, choosing, and growing on earth is ever wasted.
115.b7.p: Before speaking of the Supreme Being, the paper first names our own limits. A partial and evolving intellect could not form even its first rational thought without a frame in which to think. So the mind will postulate conclusions and invent origins, if it must, to give itself a footing. These frames are indispensable, yet without exception they are erroneous to a greater or lesser degree.
115.b8.p: That is why conceptual frames of the universe are only relatively true. God is much, much more than a Father, but the Father is man’s highest concept of God. The study of the Supreme Being begins with this honest admission.
115.b9.t: Unqualifiedly eternal, truly existential — the only level that is
A derivative, modification, and qualification of the absolute reality of infinity
The most attenuated level — it exists because God so willed
115.b11.p: From the existential standpoint, nothing new can happen anywhere, for the completion of infinity is eternally present in the seven Absolutes. Yet this fact in no way makes it impossible to realize new cosmic experiences.
115.b12.p: The key sentence of this section is this: the whole scheme of creation and evolution is a matter of the conversion of potentialities into actualities. Infinity holds much that is still only a future possibility, and the place where it becomes real is the finite world in which we live.
115.b13.t: Experiential evolution — growing and achieving in time
Experiential eventuation — emerging on a higher level
115.b15.p: No creature can grasp infinity as it is. The mind cannot form a concept without first breaking a unity into parts, so the paper presents the absolute level in three phases.
115.b16.t: The unqualified concept of the First Source and Center — the source manifestation of the I AM from which all reality takes origin
The union of the Eternal Son, the Infinite Spirit, and the Isle of Paradise — the triodity of what is already fully actual
The union of the Deity, Unqualified, and Universal Absolutes — the triodity of what is yet to be realized
115.b17.p: The interassociation of these three yields the tensions within infinity that make all universe growth possible. From the time viewpoint, the Actual is that which was and is, the Potential is that which is becoming and will be, and the Original is that which is. From the eternity viewpoint, these differences are not so apparent.
115.b19.p: Here the paper briefly comes down into our own lives. Actuals are always opening new avenues for the realization of potentials that were impossible before. The man lives in every child, and the morontia progressor is resident in the mature God-knowing man. Each of our decisions is part of cosmic growth.
115.b20.t: The Actual is what was and is; the Potential is what is becoming; the Original is what is
The differences are not apparent — in eternity all is, only not yet revealed in time and space
Actuality is substance; potentiality is capacity
115.b22.p: Any study of the origins of God the Supreme must begin with the Paradise Trinity, for the Trinity is original Deity while the Supreme is derived Deity. Yet the paper explains the source of the Supreme in two layers.
115.b23.p: The Supreme is first of all a spirit person, and this spirit person stems from the Trinity. But the Supreme is secondly a Deity of growth, and this growth derives from the two triodities, actual and potential. His identity comes from the Trinity; the drive of his growth comes from the evolution of the universe itself.
115.b24.t: The Paradise Trinity — eternal, actual, and undivided Deity
The two triodities, actual and potential — the evolution of the universes
The divinity successes of God the Sevenfold in the evolving universes
The ministry of the Conjoint Actor, who bestowed the mind of the Supreme to join power and person
115.b25.h: 5. Relation of the Supreme to the Paradise Trinity
115.b26.p: The Supreme Being depends absolutely on the existence and action of the Paradise Trinity for the reality of his personal and spirit nature. The Trinity remains forever the absolute center of perfect and infinite stability, and around it the evolutionary growth of the Supreme progressively unfolds.
115.b27.p: Growth, then, is not a matter of shaking but of turning around a center that does not move. However much our lives are shaken, the center we hold to is itself never moved.
115.b28.h: 6. Relation of the Supreme to the Triodities
115.b29.p: The Supreme grows not only as Creators and creatures become more Godlike, but also as they master the finite possibilities of the grand universe. The paper sums up this growth as a twofold motion.
115.b31.p: In the present universe age this dual motion appears as two visible streams: the Supreme Creator Personalities who go out from Paradise, and the ascending pilgrims who rise from the seven superuniverses. We ourselves stand in that inward, converging stream.
115.b32.t: How it shows in the universe
The Supreme Creator Personalities moving out into the domains of potentiality
The endless procession of ascending creatures moving toward unity with Paradise Deity
115.b34.p: In the Deity of the Supreme the Father has achieved relatively complete liberation from the limits of infinity, eternity, and absoluteness. But God the Supreme was freed only by becoming subject to the qualifications of experience. In gaining capacity for experience, he becomes subject to the need for it; in being freed from eternity, he meets the barriers of time.
115.b35.p: All this is according to the Father’s plan. That plan has predicated finite progress upon effort, creature achievement upon perseverance, and personality development upon faith. Because the Supreme was ordained in this way, finite creatures like us can exist in the universes and can someday attain the divinity of Supremacy.
115.b38.box: The Supreme Being receives his person from the Paradise Trinity, yet he is a Deity who grows through the evolutionary growth of Creators and creatures.
115.b39.p: Why did a perfect God make room for a growing Deity? Paper 115 answers: for our sake. Because the Supreme became subject to experience and growth, finite beings like us — who strive, persevere, and believe — have a place in the universe, and our growth is never in vain.
115.b41.t: Even the Father concept is relatively true — we begin in humility
Creation and evolution convert potentialities into actualities
The tension among the three phases makes all universe growth possible
His person comes from the Trinity; his growth from the two triodities
5. Relation of the Supreme to the Paradise Trinity
Growth unfolds around a center that never moves
6. Relation of the Supreme to the Triodities
A dual motion — inward convergence and outward expansion
The Father’s plan rests on effort, perseverance, and faith
116.title: The Almighty Supreme
116.b0.ask: “Why is our world so imperfect and so unequal?”
116.b2.p: Paper 115 dug into the metaphysical roots of the Supreme Being. Paper 116 now shows how this Deity works on the concrete stage where we actually live, the grand universe. The paper opens with remarkably honest words. When we look at the perfect spheres of Havona, it is reasonable to believe they were made by a perfect Creator. But anyone honest who looks at the turmoil, imperfections, and inequities of Urantia must conclude that our world was made, and is being managed, by Creators who are other than perfect.
116.b3.p: This is a great comfort to our faith. Havona did not grow, but growth characterizes the grand universe. Once we know that we live not in a finished paradise but in a place of growth, we no longer have to force ourselves to accept life’s inequalities as the will of God.
116.b7.p: It is the function of Supreme Mind to unite the power and personality attributes of Supremacy. Completed evolution will result not in a loose association of attributes but in one unified and personal Deity. From the broader perspective, there will be no Almighty apart from the Supreme, and no Supreme apart from the Almighty.
116.b8.p: The paper leaves us an unforgettable statement about mind. The body may attain completed growth, and spirit may achieve perfection of development, but mind never ceases to progress. Mind is the experiential technique of endless progress, and so the Supreme, an experiential Deity, never achieves completion of mind attainment.
116.b10.h: 2. The Almighty and God the Sevenfold
116.b11.p: God the Supreme receives his spirit and personality attributes from the Paradise Trinity, but he is actualizing his power as almighty sovereign in the doings of the Creator Sons, the Ancients of Days, and the Master Spirits. Their collective acts are the source of his growing power.
116.b12.p: Unqualified Paradise Deity is beyond the grasp of creatures of time and space. So Paradise Deity attenuates and qualifies itself, bringing into being the Supreme Creators, who carry the light of life farther and farther from Paradise. At last that light finds its most distant and beautiful expression in the earth lives of the bestowal Sons on the evolutionary worlds.
116.b13.t: God the Sevenfold — in the order mortals meet them
The experiential focus that stands between
116.b16.p: The Paradise Deities act directly in their gravity circuits, but they also work in the grand universe through three special channels. Each channel unites things that would otherwise stand apart.
116.b17.t: The mind focalizations of the Third Source and Center
Energy and spirit — mind is the vital link connecting matter and spirit
The personality revelations of the Second Source and Center
The nature of a Creator and the nature of a creature — the bestowal incarnations
The indwelling presences of the First Source and Center
Evolving creatures and God on Paradise — the Thought Adjusters
116.b18.p: On the second channel the paper says something we should never forget: when divinity becomes like humanity, inherent in that relationship is the possibility that humanity can become divine. In the very event of God becoming man, a road toward divinity opens for man.
116.b19.p: The third channel brings in the Adjuster within us. The Mystery Monitors are to human beings what the Paradise Trinity is to the Supreme Being. The Adjusters are absolute foundations, and on them our freewill choices can build an eternal nature.
116.b20.h: 4. The Almighty and the Supreme Creators
116.b21.p: The unity of the Supreme Whole depends on the progressive unification of the finite parts. During the ages when the sovereignty of Supremacy is still developing, his almighty power depends on the divinity acts of God the Sevenfold. Master Spirit Number Seven in particular speaks for the Supreme; he knows the Supreme and is in personal contact with him.
116.b22.p: The paper calls the local universes the real laboratories in which mind experiments, galactic adventures, divinity unfoldings, and personality progressions are worked out. In the local universes even the Creators evolve: the Creator Son grows from the nature of existential Paradise divinity to the experiential nature of supreme sovereignty.
116.b24.p: Here the paper turns to us. Mortal man appears to be necessary to the full function of God the Sevenfold as it culminates in the Supreme. We are not on the edge of the universe; we stand in a place its growth requires.
116.b25.h: 5. The Almighty and the Sevenfold Controllers
116.b26.p: God the Sevenfold includes not only the creators but also the controllers of the grand universe. These seven groups make up the physical-control level of this Deity association.
116.b27.t: Where the physical power potential of the Supreme is centered
Evolving as overcontroller of the physical power of the grand universe
5. The God of Action — the Infinite Spirit
The mind God, source of all controlling activity
The source and pattern of physical gravity
7. The Source of Paradise — the Universal Father
The First Source of all things
116.b28.p: The time universes are not perfect; perfection is their destiny. The struggle for perfection belongs not only to the intellectual and spiritual levels but also to the physical level of energy and mass. A growing universe is an unsettled universe, and no part of it can find real stability until the seven superuniverses are materially complete. These words offer unexpected comfort for understanding the unsteadiness of our own lives.
116.b30.p: In the evolutionary superuniverses energy-matter is dominant everywhere except in personality, where spirit, through the mediation of mind, is struggling for mastery. The goal of the evolving universes is the subjugation of energy-matter by mind and the co-ordination of mind with spirit, all through the creative and unifying presence of personality.
116.b32.p: On absolute levels energy and spirit are one, but the farther they move from Paradise, the wider the gulf between them. In the local universes they become so divergent that mind must intervene to interrelate them. Yet this very gulf creates greater opportunity. In the time-evolving universes there are more difficult problems to solve and larger opportunity to gain experience in solving them.
116.b34.h: 7. The Living Organism of the Grand Universe
116.b35.p: The last section pictures the grand universe as one body. It is not only a material creation of physical grandeur and spirit sublimity; it is also a magnificent and responsive living organism. As the human body is traversed by a network of nerve paths, the universe is penetrated by intelligence circuits; as the body is nourished by circulation, the universe is filled with energy lanes.
116.b36.t: A network of neural sensation paths
Energy lanes that activate material creation
Dependence on energies emanating from nether Paradise
Everlasting dependence on the Paradise Trinity
116.b37.p: Finally the paper ties our personal faith to the whole cosmos in a single thought. Man’s urge for Paradise perfection creates a genuine divinity tension in the living cosmos, and this tension can only be resolved by the evolution of an immortal soul. The longing of one person is part of a cosmic tension.
116.b39.box: The imperfection of our world is not a flaw in God but the mark of a universe that is growing together with Creators who are still growing.
116.b40.p: Paper 116 answers its opening question to the very end. Why is our world so imperfect and so unequal? Because the grand universe is not Havona. It is not a finished place but a place where Creators and creatures grow together. That is why faith need not become smugness for the fortunate or mere resignation for the unfortunate.
116.b42.t: Body and spirit reach completion, but mind never ceases to progress
2. The Almighty and God the Sevenfold
The Supreme stands at the center of God the Sevenfold as its experiential focus
Paradise Deity draws near through three channels: mind, bestowal, and indwelling
4. The Almighty and the Supreme Creators
The local universe is a laboratory, and mortal man is necessary
5. The Almighty and the Sevenfold Controllers
A growing universe is an unsettled universe
In personality, spirit moves toward mastery through the mediation of mind
7. The Living Organism of the Grand Universe
The grand universe is one body, and one person’s longing is part of its tension
117.title: God the Supreme
117.b0.ask: “Is the choice of one single person really written into the universe?”
117.b2.p: Paper 115 dealt with the roots of the Supreme Being and Paper 116 with the stage on which he acts. Paper 117 at last reveals how this Deity is related to each one of us. Of the three papers it is the most personal, and the closest to our daily lives.
117.b3.p: From its very first line the paper speaks to us. To the extent that we do the will of God, wherever we live in the universe, in that measure the almighty potential of the Supreme becomes one step more actual. The decision I make today to follow God’s will does not vanish somewhere; it is truly written into the growth of the evolving God.
117.b7.p: The paper lays one definition upon another. The Supreme is the beauty of physical harmony, the truth of intellectual meaning, and the goodness of spiritual value. He is the sweetness of true success and the joy of everlasting achievement. He is the oversoul of the grand universe, the consciousness of the finite cosmos, the completion of finite reality, and the personification of Creator-creature experience.
117.b8.p: In the universe procession of Creators who descend to reveal God and creatures who ascend to seek him, descenders and ascenders come to understand one another and discover an eternal brotherhood. The will of the Creator and the will of the creature are qualitatively different, but they are experientially akin. In the Supreme Being the two are united in one Deity whose will expresses one divine personality.
117.b9.t: The oversoul of the grand universe
Where all the qualities and quantities of the cosmos find their deity reflection
The consciousness of the finite cosmos
Where all that is finite comes to know itself
The greatest achievement the finite can reach
Descent and ascent meeting as one and becoming a person
117.b11.p: The Supreme is God-in-time; his is the secret of creature growth in time. To mortal man, existence is equivalent to growth. Yet this kind of growth is peculiar to the age of the Supreme’s own growth, and it will end when his growth is complete.
117.b12.p: The paper draws an interesting contrast. Beings embraced by the Trinity have experience and memory, but they do not grow as ascenders do. Through this contrast the paper looks at the incompleteness of the Supreme from an unexpected angle. Emptiness does have its virtue, for it may become experientially filled. Because he is not yet complete, there is room for beings like us to grow.
117.b13.t: Do they share in the growth?
They have experience and memory but do not grow — they belong to another universe age
Ascending mortals and other evolutionary orders
They grow — because they are in and of the Supreme and share in his cycle of growth
117.b14.h: 3. Significance of the Supreme to Universe Creatures
117.b15.p: Jesus said, “⟦Q 117:3.3⟧I am the living way,⟦/Q⟧” and so the Supreme is the living way from finite consciousness to the transcendence of consciousness. Our Creator Son can be a living channel from humanity to divinity because he actually walked that path, from the true humanity of Joshua ben Joseph to the Paradise divinity of Michael of Nebadon. In the same way the Supreme is the actual embodiment of all creature evolution and spiritualization.
117.b17.p: Man’s evolution in some ways resembles the growth of the Supreme. Man grows from the material toward the spiritual by the strength of his own decisions, and the Supreme grows in and out of the acts of the Creators. And just as the human morontia soul is a cocreative partner in its own immortalization, God the Supreme is himself a volitional, creative participant in his own deity actualization.
117.b18.t: Creates an immortal soul in partnership with the Adjuster
Actualizes his deity in liaison with the Trinity
The Adjuster is to evolving man
What the Trinity is to God the Supreme
A cocreative partner in its own immortalization
A volitional participant in his own deity actualization
117.b19.p: The Supreme did not create man, but man was literally created out of the potentiality of the Supreme. He is the very essence of evolution, and from the finite standpoint we actually live, move, and have our being within the immanence of the Supreme.
117.b21.p: God the Supreme is the finite Deity, and he must cope with the problems of the finite. Our struggles are reflections of his efforts toward self-realization. And here comes the weightiest truth of this paper. When a human being chooses eternal survival, he is cocreating destiny, and the finite God finds greater self-realization. But if a creature rejects the eternal career, that part of the Supreme which depended on this choice suffers inescapable delay.
117.b22.p: God is so trusting, so loving, that he places a portion of his divine nature in human hands for safekeeping. The individual personality may be insignificant before the whole of Supremacy, yet each human personality holds an irreplaceable meaning-value in the finite. Once it has been expressed, it never again finds identical expression except in the continuing life of that same person.
117.b24.t: He gains greater personality self-realization and enlarged experiential sovereignty
That part of him suffers inescapable delay — another may contribute later, but that will be his contribution, not mine
117.b25.p: At the end the paper asks us directly: Will you fail the God of time, who is so dependent on the decisions of the finite mind? Will you fail the great brother of all creatures? And at once it comforts us. The more closely man approaches God through love, the greater his reality. When man gives God all that he has, then God makes that man more than he is.
117.b27.p: When a creature submits to the will of the Creator, he does not submerge or surrender his personality. Rather, he is progressively enlarged by taking part in this great Deity adventure. Man does not lose his identity in union with the Supreme, but the universe repercussions of all human experience become part of the divine experience of the Supreme.
117.b28.p: When man acts, the Supreme reacts, and this transaction is the fact of progression. The circuits of energy, mind, and spirit are never the permanent possessions of the ascender; they remain forever part of the Supreme. But the character consequences of having used those circuits are what man takes with him as his own.
117.b29.t: The circuits of energy, mind, and spirit
Never the ascender’s permanent possession — forever a part of Supremacy
The character consequences of using them
Man’s own possession — decisions illuminated by worship, glorified by love, and consummated in service
The universe repercussions of all experience
Part of the divine experience of the Supreme
117.b30.p: And a wonderful compensation is promised. Being finite, creatures can never truly understand the infinite Father. But because all creature experience is registered in the Supreme, when we someday actually attain God the Supreme, that contact will include contact with total experience. The finite of time contains within itself the seeds of eternity.
117.b32.p: We seek the Supreme in the universes, but we find him not. He is the within and the without of all things; though distant, yet is he near. The Supreme is our universe home, and when we find him, it will be like returning home.
117.b34.p: Here the paper turns to the language of Father and Mother. The morontia soul of an evolving mortal is the son of the Adjuster action of the Universal Father and the child of the cosmic reaction of the Supreme Being, the Universal Mother. All soul-evolving humans are literally the evolutionary sons of God the Father and God the Mother.
117.b35.t: God the Father and the Mother Supreme
Can be discovered in our own heart — he is existential, and each ascender finds him personally
Must be sought in the hearts of all other men — found by all creatures together in the far-distant time of universal maturity
Treats each ascending son as a cosmic individual
Treats his experiential children as a single cosmic total
117.b36.p: The passage on love is the high point of the paper. All true love is from God, and man receives the divine affection as he gives this love to his fellows. Man can never take the Father’s love and imprison it in his heart; it becomes real to him only by passing through him to others. The great circuit of love is from the Father, through sons to brothers, and hence to the Supreme.
117.b37.p: Men do not find the Supreme suddenly, as an earthquake tears chasms in the rocks, but slowly and patiently, as a river quietly wears away the soil. Yet no God-knowing mortal is ever lonely on his journey, for the very way he travels is the presence of the Supreme.
117.b39.p: When all finite potentials are fully realized, the Supreme will be as discretely personalized as the Eternal Son, as concretely powerized as the Isle of Paradise, and as completely unified as the Conjoint Actor. Then the grand universe will function as a perfected whole, and the demarcations between the seven superuniverses will gradually disappear.
117.b40.p: But that completion is not the end. The thrilling adventures of organizing galaxies and evolving harmony out of chaos will rest for a while — but not for long. The enigma of the emerging Deity of God the Ultimate will challenge the perfected citizens of those universes, just as their evolutionary forebears were once challenged by the quest for God the Supreme. The curtain of cosmic destiny will draw back on a new quest for the Universal Father on higher levels.
117.b41.t: Three superfinite possibilities of the Supreme
Coinfinite participation — of which we have no satisfactory concept
117.b43.box: To the extent that we do the will of God, the Supreme becomes one step more actual. My choice is written into the universe.
117.b44.p: From beginning to end, Paper 117 answers one question: is the choice of one single person really written into the universe? The answer is yes. As we grow, the finite God grows; as we refuse, he is delayed. What greater dignity and responsibility could there be? Yet this weight does not crush us; it holds us up, for the very way we walk is his presence.
117.b46.t: He is the oversoul of the grand universe and the personification of Creator-creature experience
Emptiness has its virtue, for it may be experientially filled
3. Significance of the Supreme to Universe Creatures
Man is truly in God’s image, and his growth resembles the growth of the Supreme
The Supreme truly depends on my choice
The echoes of experience go to the Supreme; the character consequences stay with me
The Father is found in my heart; the Mother Supreme in the hearts of others
After completion, a new adventure toward the Ultimate awaits
118.title: Supreme and Ultimate—Time and Space
118.b0.ask: “Bound as we are by time and space, what place do our free choices have within God’s omnipotence and providence?”
118.b2.p: In Papers 115 through 117 we saw how the Supreme Being evolves in the universes of time and space, gathering up the experience of every creature. Now Paper 118 sets the Supreme beside the Ultimate and asks how God’s omnipotence and our freedom fit together on the stage of time and space.
118.b3.p: The author begins by setting out the seven natures of Deity. Just as God the Sevenfold is indispensable to the evolution of the Supreme, the Supreme is indispensable to the emergence of the Ultimate; together they form the experiential bridge linking the beginnings and the completions of all creative growth in the master universe. Creative growth is unending, yet it is punctuated by satisfying moments of goal attainment, which serve as preludes to new adventures.
118.b4.p: How, then, do we who live in time taste eternity? If God is all-powerful, why are our choices real? And how does providence work in our lives?
118.b9.p: In the evolving universes, eternity is the everlasting now. A mortal may become eternal by identifying himself with the indwelling spirit through choosing to do the will of the Father. Once purpose is fixed in this way, a million or a billion moments make no difference; number has ceased to have meaning for that purpose.
118.b10.p: Maturity is directly related to the unit of time consciousness. The mature self brings past experience and future wisdom to bear on present decisions; it lives more intensely in the present while escaping the limits of the present. Patience is exercised by those whose time units are short; true maturity transcends patience by a forbearance born of real understanding.
118.b11.t: Concentrates meaning into the present moment, cut off from past and future
Sees past, present, and future together and gains insight into the wholeness of events
The present moment contains all of the past and all of the future
118.b13.p: The ubiquity of Deity — his being everywhere — must not be confused with the ultimacy of divine omnipresence. The Father wills that the Supreme, the Ultimate, and the Absolute should complement and unify his presence. God the Supreme is literally a manifestation of divine ubiquity: between the spiritual presence of the Creator and the material manifestations of creation lies a vast domain of the ubiquitous becoming.
118.b14.t: Progressively, through the ministry of God the Sevenfold
We find him as a person
We attempt to know him as Ultimate, and then begin the quest of the Absolute
118.b15.p: No finaliter will be disturbed by the uncertainties of seeking the Absolute, for he has already met God the Father. Even if finaliters should find God the Absolute, they will only be discovering the same Paradise Father, revealing himself on more universal levels.
118.b17.p: Time is a succession of instants, and space is a system of associated points. We perceive time by analysis and space by synthesis, and we join the two through the integrating insight of personality. Of all the animal world, only man has this time-space perceptibility.
118.b18.p: Things are bound by time, but truth is timeless. The more truth we know and the more truth we are, the more of the past we can understand and of the future we can comprehend. When the eternal truth of the Creator is linked with the finite experience of the creature, a new value of the Supreme emerges. Space comes nearer than any other nonabsolute thing to being absolute, but that does not mean it is absolute.
118.b21.p: Many theological difficulties arise because men assign infinite and absolute attributes to subordinate and evolutionary Deity. There is indeed a true First Cause, but there is also a host of co-ordinate and subordinate causes.
118.b22.t: Original effects, free of inheritance from any earlier cause
Effects that always inherit something from preceding causes
118.b23.t: By the mandate of the Trinity, the Deity Absolute acts in and upon the Unqualified Absolute
The agencies of Ultimacy transform undifferentiated potentials into defined plans
3. Creation and evolution of universe actuals
The Supreme Creators turn matured potentials into experiential actuals
118.b24.p: In the cosmic sense the Creator Sons are transformative creators, but this does not make our idea of them as creators wrong. From the finite viewpoint, they certainly can and do create.
118.b26.p: Omnipotence does not mean the power to do what cannot be done. Even the infinite God cannot create square circles or produce evil that is inherently good. God cannot do the ungodlike thing. For omnipotence not only creates things; it gives origin to the very nature of all things and beings.
118.b27.p: In the beginning the Father does all, but as eternity unfolds it becomes clear that creatures, even men, are to become God’s partners. And this is true even in the life in the flesh: when man and God enter into partnership, no limit can be placed on its future possibilities.
118.b30.p: God is truly omnipotent, but he is not omnificent — he does not personally do all that is done. To claim that primal Deity personally does everything would disenfranchise nearly a million Creator Sons and countless other creative helpers. There is but one uncaused Cause in the whole universe, yet this in no way violates the free will of the children of Deity.
118.b31.p: All volition is relative. Man cannot choose to be other than a human being, but he can elect to become more than a man. The range of human will is strictly finite, with one exception: when man chooses to find God and to be like him, that choice is superfinite. To recognize God’s omnipotence gives security, but to accept the fallacy of omnificence is to embrace the colossal error of pantheism.
118.b34.p: The maximum limits foreordained by the Master Architects do not in the least reduce the sovereignty of creature will within those limits. A mature adult may accurately foresee the decision of a younger person, yet this foreknowledge takes nothing away from the freedom of the decision. In the same way, God’s foreknowledge does not abolish finite will.
118.b35.p: Error in choosing is possible only in time, and sin is immaturity dazzled by the freedom of the will while failing to see the duties of cosmic citizenship. If personality is truly free, the possibility of self-destruction cannot be avoided. So choice is narrowed for safety on the lower levels, and it becomes increasingly free as the universes are ascended.
118.b36.t: Self-determination, self-evolution, and self-identification with a fusion spirit of Deity
118.b38.p: Man is a living mechanism, but much more than a machine: he is mind endowed and spirit indwelt. He can never escape the chemical and electrical mechanics of his body, but by consecrating his mind to the urges of the Adjuster he can learn to subordinate it to the wisdom of experience. The spirit liberates, and the mechanism limits, the function of will.
118.b39.t: Stability is secured at the expense of progress
Choice uncontrolled by mechanism and unidentified with spirit
Liberation from the physical level together with divine stability
118.b40.p: External restraints such as time and space, hunger and fear, limit the choices of immature man, and the slowness of evolution is a brake against dangerous speeds of progress. When material achievement outruns the growth of worship-wisdom, civilization carries the seeds of its own retrogression. The iniquity of Caligastia, and of Lucifer, lay in breaking down this time governor. For every restraint he transcends, man must take on a new and voluntary restraint — concepts of justice and ideals of brotherhood.
118.b42.p: Time and space are a conjoined mechanism of the master universe, the devices that allow finite creatures to coexist with the Infinite. Without them no creature could act, but by them every creature’s acts are limited. Man does not have unfettered free will, but within the range of his choice his will is relatively sovereign.
118.b43.p: The grand universe is mechanism as well as organism, and mechanisms are the fixed crystallizations of Creator thought. They should not be thought of as limiting Deity; rather, in these very mechanics Deity has achieved one phase of eternal expression. God the Supreme is the personalization of all universe experience and the focalization of all finite evolution, and in the eternal future he will synthesize the diversities of the finite into one meaningful whole.
118.b45.p: Providence does not mean that God has decided all things for us in advance. God loves us too much to do that, for that would be cosmic tyranny, and divine love is not a shortsighted affection that would pamper and spoil us. Providence works with regard to the whole: it is the importance of a creature’s function to some total — a race, a nation, a planet — that occasions providential intervention, not the importance of the creature as a person. Nevertheless, the Father as a person may at any time interpose a fatherly hand.
118.b46.p: What we call providence is often the product of chance, and what we call good luck may really be bad luck. The apparent cruelty of a hard fate may in reality be the tempering fire that turns the soft iron of immature personality into the tempered steel of real character. The view that natural law is heartless is modified in three ways as humanity progresses.
118.b47.t: A growing grasp of facts, meanings, and ideals
Accumulated knowledge of material laws and spiritual purposes
Closer harmony with the Supreme, so that providence becomes an actuality
118.b48.p: Providence is partial because the Supreme is not yet complete, and unpredictable because creature attitudes keep changing. When we pray for providential intervention, many times the answer is our own changed attitude toward life. Providence is not whimsical or magical; it is the slow and sure emergence of the sovereign of the finite universes.
118.b51.p: Paper 118 shows the stage of time and space as both a limit and a gift. Time and space shield us from the Infinite and pace our immature choices so that they do not destroy us. God is omnipotent but does not personally do all things; he foreknows, yet he does not take away our choices. Within these limits our will is real, and the choice to find God and be like him reaches beyond the finite. Providence is not a script written in advance but the sure march of the Supreme as he slowly emerges, and as we mature spiritually we begin to see harmony in what once looked like chaos.
118.b52.t: When we choose the Father’s will, our purpose in time becomes eternal
God the Supreme is a manifestation of divine ubiquity
Things are bound by time, but truth is timeless
There is one First Cause, but countless subordinate causes work with it
God cannot do the ungodlike thing
God is omnipotent but does not personally do all that is done
God’s foreknowledge does not abolish the freedom of our choices
Spirit liberates the will; transcended restraints are replaced by restraints of wisdom
Time and space let the finite coexist with the Infinite
Providence is not a fixed script but the sure emergence of the Supreme
118.b54.box: Within time and space our choices are real, and the choice to seek God reaches beyond the finite into eternity.
